diagnosis.headline: Checkouts failed for a while because payment could not be reached (checkout→payment DNS lookup failures; the payment container was restarted at 08:47:24). Payment has recovered and orders are going through again. One unexplained signal is still active: 100% of ad's outgoing client calls fail, though ad keeps serving.

root_causes.cause: The payment container was down, then started again at 08:47:24 (restart_count 0, so it was stopped/started or recreated, not crash-looping; not OOM: oom_killed=false). While it was gone, Docker DNS could not resolve 'payment', so checkout's Charge calls failed with 'lookup payment on 127.0.0.11:53: server misbehaving' and orders failed. It has since recovered: checkout→payment calls now reach payment server spans, checkout logs 'payment went through', and checkout has had no error traces in the last 4m.

Users saw 'Checkout failed to place order' (logged at 08:48:40) while payment was unreachable.
Unreachable by name for a while (container restarted at 08:47:24, memory series dropped to 0). Now running and serving Charge calls again.
All of ad's outgoing client calls fail (client_error_rate 1.0). Its server error rate is 0 and it keeps serving ad requests, so impact on users is small or none.
A few error spans (3 in 5m, on 'router frontend egress', no message). Requests now mostly return 200.

ruled_out.reason: No error traces in 15m. Memory is high but flat (no growth or OOM). It was only reporting checkout's failure.
The failures started in its calls to payment (DNS lookup of payment), not in checkout's own logic, and it has had no errors in the last 4m.

open_questions: Which callee do ad's failing client calls go to, and what is the error? It is not visible in the Jaeger edges (E5); check ad's client spans directly.
Who or what stopped or restarted payment at 08:47:24? Exit code 0 and oom_killed=false (E19) point to a deliberate stop or recreate rather than a crash.
The frontend-proxy error spans (E16) have no message. Check whether they come from the payment outage or from something else.
Frontend memory is at 93.76% of its 250 MB limit (flat, E11). It is not part of this incident but should be watched.
Product-catalog latency is about 600–900 ms on the server side (E15/E18) but is not flagged against its baseline. Confirm this is normal.
prevention: Find out why the payment container was stopped or recreated at 08:47:24 (manual action, compose redeploy, or host event). Add an alert on container restarts and missing payment spans so checkout failures are caught before users report them.
Add retry/backoff on checkout→payment for transient name-resolution failures, and keep a health-check-based restart policy on payment.
Add an alert on client_error_rate per service so cases like ad's failing outgoing calls are seen early.

objections.text: The timing doesn't fit the claim that DNS failed 'while it was gone'. Payment restarted about 648–671 s before the checks, roughly 08:47:00–08:47:30. The only frontend checkout failure was logged at 08:48:40, more than a minute after payment was running and healthy again. The DNS failures may continue after the container came back. That points to something else: payment detached from the Docker network, embedded DNS trouble, or a second outage. E14 gives no timestamps, so we can't tell whether the 20 failing traces fall before or after the restart.

Some recovery claims have no registered evidence behind them. Nothing in the evidence contains a checkout log saying 'payment went through'. E18 only shows that 10 checkout->payment calls reached payment server spans. It doesn't show they succeeded or when they happened. E17 covers only 240 s. Calling payment 'resolved' therefore rests on thin evidence.

The diagnosis ignores E16: 3 of 3 traces fail at frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress', and that is the service the alert is about. Proxy-to-frontend egress failures can't be explained by checkout->payment DNS. They could be a separate user-facing cause, so they should be explained or ruled out.

E18 is cited as support, but the checkout->payment client/server latency gap (about 105 ms) matches the checkout->shipping gap (about 83 ms, E15), and shipping isn't implicated at all. The gap looks like normal overhead, not a sign tied to payment.

Payment logged no warn+ lines in 600 s (E8), which covers the restart window. Nothing shows why payment stopped or what restarted it. The memory series (E13) is described as flat, but it drops to 0 and climbs to 67.7%. That fits a restart but tells us nothing about the cause. So the 'origin' is really a symptom, and what actually drove it is unknown.

alternative_root_cause.component: payment network attachment / Docker embedded DNS
alternative_root_cause.reason: DNS lookups for 'payment' apparently kept failing after the container restarted and showed healthy. That fits payment being missing from the Docker network or a DNS fault better than the container simply being stopped. Separately, the frontend-proxy egress failures (E16) are still unexplained.
